data.name: The Old City: Leviathan
data.detailed_description:
The Old City: Leviathan is an experiment in first person exploration that focuses entirely on story.

Everything else is secondary. All that exists is you and the world. Set in a decaying city from a civilization long past, The Old City: Leviathan puts the player in the shoes of a sewer dwelling isolationist. You progress through the narrative by simply exploring the world. The story itself is told via the musings of your character and, chiefly, the environment itself. This environment has been designed to be diverse, interesting, and meaningful to the narrative of the game.

The objective is to understand. The story of The Old City: Leviathan is not told in a traditional manner. As you progress through the narrative, you will overhear a conversation between two entities. The first entity is the nameless character you are controlling who communicates through a monologue. The second entity is the depths of the environment, details and all. Your task is to piece together the narrative as if you are jumping into a conversation with no context. The more you explore, the more you will potentially understand.

This experience is not a normal one.

reviews.review:
You have of course been to the beach, but have you ever considered the two paths that there lie before you?

One, is to sunbathe. Keeping yourself within the understood. Perhaps it is boring, but not enough for it to be an issue. Should you be the type of person inclined to choose this option. The calm of predictability is after all what you are seeking. The boredom and sanity are one, in this sense. If that's the case, I don't know that this game has much to offer you (beyond a shift in perspective you currently don't desire).

The other option, is to venture out into the water. Will it be cold at first? Most definitely. That is what keeps some sunbathing, I think. Will you grow accustomed to the cold? In part, but always it will return, your body telling you that, should you stay too long, you will depart completely. Why do it then? Why venture into the painful & deadly? That which may only be endured, not enjoyed? Conviction. Conviction that the suffering will yield something, with an immense value. The belief that you can do much more than mere pleasure would limit your capacity to. That there is a purpose that lies beyond [i] yourself [/i], [i] your creed [/i], [i] your capacity [/i]. And so, in striving for it, you will incorporate it, and be worth all the more. If this is your dream, if you feel a deep stirring within as you understand the meaning of these words, then -just as it does for me- The Old City calls for you. Heed its call; let Leviathan bolster your being, so that Nineveh may be cured. What other path is there? Not one worth pondering, surely... The unclean waters are a heavy burden to shoulder alone, without ice.

The exploratory narrative and pages intentionally left blank (to let the intensity of the former breathe) may admittedly interrupt the flow and lead to tedium, if one is not sufficiently in tune with the games dense and poetic prose (and falling out of tune is a tragic and fairly frequent possibility). It should be approached as a scavenger hunt instead of as a sermon, I'd ironically preach. And if one is unwilling to engage with some rather dark and gruesome themes, then one best steer clear. Though I would uninvitedly caution you from closing your eyes too much: those dark sights hold beauty in abundance too.

A rosary and love letter to the agnostic spirit, The Old City: Leviathan is a philosophical and spiritual work that appears masterful in symbols and rich in meaning. An experience that calls for me to return and wander, both in body and mind.
